en: Abaca fibers are used to make strong Manila ropes because they possess exceptional tensile strength and resist saltwater damage.
Sulfur dioxide gas escapes from Taal Volcano's main crater, demonstrating how matter exists as an invisible gas at high temperatures.
Shaved ice in a bowl of halo-halo undergoes a physical change from solid to liquid as it absorbs environmental heat.
The natural fermentation of coconut sap into tuba involves a chemical change where yeast converts sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
Tamarind extract dissolves in boiling water to create the sour broth of sinigang, forming a homogeneous liquid mixture called a solution.
Capiz shells are translucent rather than transparent, allowing light to pass through them diffusely to create soft glows in traditional windows.
Salt farmers in Dasol, Pangasinan use solar evaporation to physically separate solid salt crystals from liquid seawater mixtures.
The bright paint on old jeepneys eventually chips, exposing iron metal to oxygen and moisture to form reddish-brown rust.
Molten lava flowing down Mayon Volcano cools and solidifies into hard rock, changing from a liquid to a solid state.
A bowl of lugaw is a heterogeneous mixture because its solid rice grains and liquid broth remain visibly distinct.
Bamboo stems bend during strong typhoons without breaking because their cellular structure provides high flexibility, a valuable physical property.
Unripe Guimaras mangoes turn yellow and sweet as they ripen due to chemical changes that convert starches into simpler sugars.
